Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:11:1.hebrew: חלקת בו בין תם למועד - דמועד משלם כופר, ותם פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:11:1.english: You distinguished in it between an innocuous [ox] and a forewarned [ox] - For a forewarned [ox] pays ransom, and an innocuous [ox] is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:12:1.hebrew: חלקת בו בין תם למועד - דמועד משלם כופר, ותם פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:12:1.english: You distinguished regarding him between an innocuous [ox] and a forewarned [ox] - For a forewarned [ox] pays ransom, and an innocuous [ox] is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:12:2.hebrew: שאינו נותן אלא שלשים - אפילו שוה ק' מנה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:12:2.english: Where he gives only thirty - Even if [the slave] is worth a hundred maneh.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:14:1.english: And it killed a man, etc. - [This] is written regarding a forewarned [ox].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:15:1.english: Her injuries [go] to her heirs - and not to her husband.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:16:1.hebrew: [וירש אותה] - ונתתם את נחלתו לשארו הקרוב אליו וגו' — שארו זו אשתו. והא ליכא למימר דלדידה ניתיב ירושה דידיה, דהא ממשפחתו כתיב. אלא ה"ק: ונתתם את נחלתו לקרוב אליו ממשפחתו, ושארו — שהיא אשתו — הוא יורש אותה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:16:1.english: [And he shall inherit her] - [The verse states:] "Then you shall give his inheritance to his she'ero [next of kin] who is closest to him, etc." — his she'ero [refers to] his wife. And it is impossible to say that we should give his inheritance to her, for "from his family" is written [there]. Rather, this is what [the verse] is saying: "Then you shall give his inheritance to the one closest to him from his family," and [as for] his she'ero — who is his wife — he inherits her.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:17:1.hebrew: לא אמר ר"ע - נזקיה ליורשיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:17:1.english: Rabbi Akiva did not say - [that] her damages [go] to her heirs.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:17:2.hebrew: אלא - בכופר, הואיל ואין משתלם אלא לאחר מיתתה. הלכך, לא זכתה בו מחיים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:17:2.english: Only - with regard to ransom, since it is paid only after her death. Therefore, she did not acquire it during her lifetime.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:17:3.hebrew: והוה ליה ראוי - ולא מוחזק. וקיימא לן ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קיג.) דאין הבעל יורש את אשתו בראוי לבוא לאחר מיתתה כבמוחזק לה מחיים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:17:3.english: And it is [considered] prospective [property] - and not [property] in [her] possession. And we hold in [chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 113a) that a husband does not inherit his wife in [property] due to come after her death as [he does] in [property] possessed by her during [her] lifetime.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:18:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא - אין כופר משתלם אלא לאחר מיתה? אע"ג דכתיב "והמית", נימא דכיון שאמדוהו למיתה, לישתלם מחיים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:18:1.english: What is the reason - [that] ransom is paid only after death? Even though it is written "and it killed," might we say that since they assessed him [as destined] to die, it should be paid while [he is] alive?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:18:2.hebrew: [והמית כו'] - שור אינו בסקילה עד שימות הניזק, דכתיב "והמית איש והשור יסקל":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:18:2.english: [And it killed, etc.] - An ox is not [subject] to stoning until the injured [party] dies, as it is written: "And it killed a man... and the ox shall be stoned."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:1:1.hebrew: ונימא ר"ע לנפשיה - כדאקשי ליה לר' אליעזר לעיל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:1:1.english: And let Rabbi Akiva say to himself - Just as he objected to Rabbi Eliezer above.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:20:1.hebrew: ודמי ולדות לבעל - התורה זכתה לו, כדכתיב בעל האשה (שמות כא):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:20:1.english: And compensation for [miscarried] offspring to the husband - The Torah awarded [it] to him, as it is written, "the woman's husband" (Exodus 21).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:20:2.english: [If] the woman is not [alive, he] gives to her heirs - [Compensation for] damage and pain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:20:3.hebrew: היתה שפחה ונשתחררה כו' - כלומר, היתה משוחררת מעוברת ממשוחרר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:20:3.english: [If] she was a maidservant and was emancipated, etc. - That is to say, she was an emancipated [woman] pregnant by an emancipated [man].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:2:1.hebrew: כשקדם בעליו ושחטו - קודם שנגמר דינו, אצטריך ליה קרא למפטריה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:2:1.english: Where its owner slaughtered it first - before its verdict was finalized, the verse was needed to exempt him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:3:1.hebrew: אי הכי - אמאי מותיב ר"ע לרבי אליעזר לעיל הביאהו לב"ד, ולא אסיק אדעתיה דמצי לשנויי ליה כשקדם ושחטו, אי לית ליה טעמא אחרינא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:3:1.english: If so - why did Rabbi Akiva raise the objection to Rabbi Eliezer above, "Bring it to court," and it did not occur to him that [Rabbi Eliezer] could answer him [that it refers to a case] where [the owner] slaughtered it first, if [Rabbi Akiva] did not have another reason?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:5:1.hebrew: אמר לך - ר' אליעזר, שקדם ושחטו לא אצטריך קרא; דהתם כי הרגו שלא בכוונה, אצטריך למפטריה מכופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:5:1.english: He [would] say to you - Rabbi Eliezer [would say]: [For a case where] he slaughtered it first, a verse is not needed; for there, when it killed him unintentionally, [a verse] is needed to exempt him from ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:5:2.hebrew: דשור לאו בר קטלא הוא כלל - ואי לא מיעטיה, הוה אמינא עיקר חיובו כופר הוא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:5:2.english: Since the ox is not subject to be killed at all - And if [the verse] had not excluded him, I would have said [that] his primary obligation is ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:5:3.hebrew: אבל הכא - דשור בר קטלא הוא, תחילת דינו נפטר מממון ולא חלה עליו תשלומין, דאיכא למימר הביאהו לב"ד. הלכך, כי קדים ושחטו נמי, בלא קרא מיפטר ולא צריך קרא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:5:3.english: But here - since the ox is subject to be killed, [from] the outset of its judgment it is exempt from monetary [liability] and payment does not take effect upon it, for one can say: "Bring it to the court." Therefore, even when [the owner] slaughters it first, it is exempt without a verse, and a verse is not needed.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:6:1.hebrew: לר"ע נמי ודאי הכי הוא - קושיא היא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:6:1.english: According to Rabbi Akiva also, certainly it is so - This is a question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:7:1.hebrew: נשלם דמי עבד מעלייה - ואע"ג דמקטיל, דהא לגבי חבלת אדם אין תורת תם עליו ואינו נפטר בטענת הביאהו לב"ד — כתב רחמנא נקי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:7:1.english: The value of a slave is paid from superior-quality [property] - Even though [the ox] is killed, since with respect to injuring a person the law of an innocuous [ox] does not apply to it, and [the owner] is not exempted by the claim of "Bring it to court" — the Merciful One wrote: "[The owner of the ox] shall be clear."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:8:1.hebrew: והא תבריה רבי עקיבא לגזיזיה - דאשמעינן בהדיא דאין משתלם אלא מגופו, ואכתי איכא למימר "הביאהו לב"ד":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:8:1.english: But didn't Rabbi Akiva break his fist - For he explicitly taught us that [compensation] is paid only from its body, and one can still say, "Bring it to the court."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 42b:9:1.english: Since I am more stringent regarding a slave - With regard to a forewarned [ox].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:11:1.hebrew: מה כשחייב בן חורין חלקת בין תם למועד - ברייתא זו מוכחא דר"ע לא קבל תשובה דר"א, דהא לא דריש ר"ע נקי מחצי כופר, ואפילו הכי פוטר כאן בתם; והיינו משום דכי לא מיחייב סקילה, פשיטא דפטור מכופר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:11:1.english: Just as when [the Torah] deemed [him] liable [for] a freeman, you distinguished between an innocuous [ox] and a forewarned [ox] - This baraita proves that Rabbi Akiva did not accept Rabbi Eliezer's reply, for Rabbi Akiva does not expound [the verse as teaching that he is] clear from half a ransom, and even so he exempts [him] here in [the case of] an innocuous [ox]; and this is because when [the ox] is not liable to stoning, it is obvious that [the owner] is exempt from ransom.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:13:1.hebrew: נקי מדמי עבד - פירוש: משלשים של עבד, ויש מפרשים דאפילו דמים לא משלם, וכ"ש קנס:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:13:1.english: Clear from [paying] compensation for a slave - Explanation: [Clear] from the thirty [sela] of a slave; and some explain that he does not even pay [the slave's actual] value, and all the more so [not] the fine.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:17:1.hebrew: והוה ליה ראוי - אף על גב דביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קיג.) דריש דאין הבעל נוטל בראוי כבמוחזק מקרא אחרינא, מהכא לא נפקא, דהוה אמינא דשאני כופר דלעולם הוי ראוי, ולא אתי מיניה שאר ראוי. וכופר נמי לא נפיק מהתם, דהתם בירושה שנפלה לאחר מיתת האשה אין הבעל נוטל בראוי; אבל כופר, דמחיים נעשה החבלה שהכופר בא על ידה, הוה אמינא דנוטל:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:17:1.english: And it is [considered property] due - Even though in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 113a) [the Gemara] derives from another verse that a husband does not take in [property] due [to his wife] as [he does] in [property she] possessed, [that rule] could not be derived from here; for I would say that ransom is different because it is always [only] due [after death], and [therefore] other [types of property] due would not be derived from it. And ransom, too, could not be derived from there, for there, it is regarding an inheritance that fell [to her] after the wife's death [that] the husband does not take in [property] due; whereas [regarding] ransom, where the injury on account of which the ransom comes was inflicted during [her] lifetime, I would say that he does take [it].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:1:1.hebrew: ונימא רבי עקיבא לנפשיה - ולא בעי למימר שלא היה יודע אותם תירוצים, וכשאמר לו רבי אליעזר קבלם, דפשוט לו לגמרא דמסתמא היה יודע, ומה שלא היה חושש — משום דאית ליה דרבה, דאי אין השור בסקילה אין הבעלים משלמים כופר. וא"ת: ודלמא "אם כופר" לא דריש, ו"אם עבד" דריש? וי"ל: כיון דלא דריש "אם כופר", כ"ש דלא דריש "אם עבד", כדמוכח לקמן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:1:1.english: But let Rabbi Akiva say to himself - And [the Gemara] does not want to say that [Rabbi Akiva] did not know those answers and that when Rabbi Eliezer told [them] to him, he accepted them, for it is obvious to the Gemara that he presumably knew [them], and that the reason he was not concerned [about this difficulty] is because he holds [the view] of Rabbah, that if the ox is not [subject to] stoning, the owners do not pay ransom. And if you say: Perhaps he does not expound "if a ransom," while he does expound "if a slave"? And one can answer: Since he does not expound "if a ransom," all the more so he does not expound "if a slave," as is proven later on:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:20:1.hebrew: נותן נזק וצער לאשה - נקט נזק וצער לפי שרגילות הוא שמצטערת יותר, וגם נפחתין דמיה כשמפלת ע"י הכאה מכשיולדת בזמנה; אבל ריפוי ושבת — אורחא דמילתא הוא שאין צריכה ריפוי, וגם אינה מתבטלת יותר ממלאכה משאר יולדת, וכזה היה סופה כשתלד. וא"ת: ובושת מ"ט לא חשיב? וי"ל: נתכוין לבייש זה ובייש זה פטור לר"ש בהחובל (לקמן בבא קמא דף פו.), ומיירי דנתכוון להכות חבירו והכה האשה כפשטיה דקרא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:20:1.english: He gives [compensation for] damage and pain to the woman - [The baraita] specified damage and pain because it is usual that she suffers more pain and her value is also diminished when she miscarries due to a blow than when she gives birth at her [due] time; whereas [as for] medical expenses and loss of livelihood — the normal course of things is that she does not need medical treatment, and she is also not idled from work any more than any other woman giving birth, and such would have been her outcome [anyway] when she gave birth. And if you ask: why did it not list humiliation? One can answer: [If] one intended to humiliate this [person] and humiliated that [other person], he is exempt according to Rabbi Shimon in [the chapter] HaChovel (below, Bava Kamma 86a), and [the baraita] is dealing with a case where he intended to strike his fellow and struck the woman, like the plain meaning of the verse.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:20:2.hebrew: היתה שפחה ונשתחררה או גיורת זכה - פ"ה: נתעברה מן הגר ומן המשוחרר. וכן משמע בהפרה (לקמן בבא קמא דף מט.), דקאמר: "לא שנו אלא שחבל בה בחיי הגר". ואין לומר כריב"א, שנתעברה בעודה שפחה — דאין לבעל כלום, דשל אדון נינהו — ועכשיו נשתחררה, כדמשמע לישנא ד"היתה שפחה"; דהא בהפרה (שם) משמע כדפ"ה. והא דנקט "היתה שפחה ונשתחררה" ולא נקט "היתה משוחררת", משום דע"כ כשאין לה בנים קאמר, ולהכי נקט "ונשתחררה", דמשמע עתה מקרוב. וה"ה לישראלית נשואה לגר ומת הגר, דפטור, דהא דמי ולדות לבעלה. והא דנקט שפחה וגיורת, משום דאורחא דמילתא כך, דסתם משוחררת נשואה למשוחרר, וסתמא גיורת לגר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:20:2.english: If she was a maidservant and was emancipated, or a convert, he gains - Rashi explained: She conceived from a convert or from an emancipated [slave]. And so it is implied in [chapter] HaParah (below, Bava Kamma 49a), where it states: "They taught this only where he injured her during the lifetime of the convert." And one should not say like Riba, that she conceived while she was still a maidservant — for the husband has nothing, since [the offspring] belong to the master — and now she was emancipated, as the wording "she was a maidservant" implies; for in [chapter] HaParah (ibid.) it is implied as Rashi explained. And the reason [the baraita] stated "she was a maidservant and was emancipated" and did not state "she was an emancipated woman" is because perforce it is speaking of a case where she has no children, and therefore it stated "and was emancipated," which implies [that it happened] just now, recently. And the same law applies to a Jewish woman [by birth] who is married to a convert and the convert died [without heirs], that [the assailant] is exempt, for compensation for offspring belongs to her husband. And the reason it specifically mentioned a [freed] maidservant and a convert is because that is the usual way of things: for an emancipated maidservant is ordinarily married to an emancipated slave, and a female convert is ordinarily [married] to a male convert.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:7:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב אסי כו' - וא"ת: ומה דוחקו לתרץ? נימא דגם ר"ע היה יודע וסובר אותו תירוץ שהשיב לו ר"א, וסבר דלמא אית ליה טעמא אחרינא, כדאמר לעיל אקדם ושחטו. וי"ל: דגבי טעם דקדם ושחטו שייך לומר הכי, שאינו טעם טוב כדפרישית לעיל; אבל אטעם דהמית על פי עד אחד וגבי טעמא דנתכוין, לא שייך למימר דלמא אית ליה טעמא אחרינא, דטעמים חשובין הן וליכא למפרך עליהו מידי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:7:1.english: "Rather, Rav Asi said," etc. - And if you ask: What forced him [Rav Asi] to answer [as he did]? Let us say that Rabbi Akiva also knew and held that same answer that Rabbi Eliezer replied to him, and [Rabbi Akiva] thought, "Perhaps he has another reason," just as [the Gemara] said above regarding [the case where the owner] slaughtered it first. And one can answer that regarding the reason of "he slaughtered it first," it is appropriate to say this, for it is not a good reason, as I explained above; however, regarding the reason of "it killed [on the testimony of] one witness" and regarding the reason of "it intended [to kill another animal]," it is not appropriate to say "perhaps he has another reason," for they are substantial reasons and there is nothing to refute against them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:9:1.hebrew: ועבד יפה סלע נותן ל' - אע"ג דשוה ק', אין נותן אלא שלשים; מ"מ כיון שנותן קצבה של שלשים אע"פ שאין שוה אלא סלע או יותר — שלעולם הקצבה עומדת — א"כ גם כשהשור אין שוה כלום, קיימת:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 42b:9:1.english: And [in the case of] a slave worth a sela, he gives thirty - Even though [the slave] is worth a hundred [selas], he gives only thirty; nevertheless, since he gives a fixed amount of thirty even if [the slave] is worth only a sela or more — for the fixed amount always stands — if so, even when the ox is worth nothing, [the fixed amount] still stands.
